newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rises on strong state demand.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rises on strong state demand.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose a few more basis points on Wednesday as the state was still searching for liquidity to pay salaries and subsidies.
"The state is not only bringing Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) into the market, but is also a big buyer of call in its effort to collect liquidity," said one dealer.
Another said the governemnt was near the end of its search for liquidity, adding call rates could come down on Thursday.
Call rates, trading at 2.81/87 bid in morning trade on Wednesday, are likely to slip to 2.75/81 bid on Thursday, dealers said.
Most business was done at the shorter end as most traders did not want to go beyond the year-end.
One-month deposits were unchanged at 2.80 percent bid and three-month paper slipped two basis points to 2.82 percent bid.
The guilder was virtually unchanged at 112.17 per 100 marks from 112.175 on Tuesday.
